core.title: An unexamined docs corpus is COULD_NOT_CHECK, never PASS or FAIL
core.given: The docs validation capability is run over the corpus.
core.when: The toolchain is absent, the renderer crashes, the tree is unreadable, or a build failure cannot be attributed to a specific document.
core.then: The verdict MUST be COULD_NOT_CHECK, which BLOCKS. It is reported as a named state that reaches the report: never PASS, never FAIL, never NOT_APPLICABLE.
prefer: For COULD_NOT_CHECK, restore the missing rendering toolchain and re-run, rather than suppressing the verdict
avoid: Treating a missing rendering toolchain as a clean corpus. It is an unexamined one.
Collapsing COULD_NOT_CHECK (blocks) into NOT_APPLICABLE (permits) or PASS
'Fixing' COULD_NOT_CHECK by making the validation capability return PASS when the renderer is absent
Turning an unresolvable lookup into an empty clean result
core.why: The verdict distinction is the point of this rule and the thing most likely to be got wrong: collapsing 'I could not observe whether the obligation was met' into 'clean' is a defect that has been re-committed more than once.
evidence: When the toolchain is absent or the failure is unattributable, the validation capability's report shows COULD_NOT_CHECK (not PASS, FAIL or NOT_APPLICABLE) and the gate blocks
verification: Scope: a render failure the capability cannot pin to a document — a crashed renderer, an unreadable tree, or a rendering toolchain that is not installed — is COULD_NOT_CHECK, which BLOCKS.
Verdict mapping: an ABSENT toolchain, or a build failure the capability cannot attribute to a specific document, is COULD_NOT_CHECK — never PASS and never FAIL.

The verdict distinction is the point of this rule: 'there is no obligation here' (NOT_APPLICABLE, permits) and 'I could not see whether the obligation was met' (COULD_NOT_CHECK, blocks) must never collapse into one another.
An unresolvable lookup must remain DATA: a named, reportable state that reaches the report, never an empty clean result.
The collapse is a recurring defect pattern: a check that reports PASS (or degrades to advisory) when it cannot observe is a defect of the check, not a clean result.
Severity 1. Disposition strict: fails on every finding; no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.

fires: The validation capability runs where the rendering toolchain is not installed
The renderer crashes or the document tree is unreadable
A build failure cannot be attributed to a specific document
A plan artifact, acceptance or validator design defines what the gate reports when it cannot observe
doesNotFire: A build failure attributed to a specific document; that is FAIL under the companion rule that requires the corpus to render
An unresolved internal reference; that is FAIL under the companion rule that requires internal references to resolve

bunOnly.text: Defect lineage. Spec 2 §3 states this emphatically because the repository has the bug in at least three places. In #1745, coach.pr.merge-blocks-on-pre-smoke-close degrades to advisory on a lookup failure and REPORTS IT AS A PASS. In #1774, 'no mirror found' is read as 'nothing to lose', and 15 nodes are invisible to the succession guard. In #1716, checks pass when they cannot observe, and C011 compares the store against itself.
bunOnly.reason: Named historical incidents, rule ids and check ids of this repository; only the generic lesson (a check that reports clean when it cannot observe is defective) is stack-neutral.

neutralityNotes: The obligation is pure gate semantics (which verdict a validation capability must report when it cannot observe) and is fully stack-neutral; no profile key is needed. The corpus scope is deferred to the capability's configuration exactly as the Bun text does ('the configured corpus'), so no roots/suffix key is required. Bun-only residue: the rendering toolchain's identity and install command (asciidoctor, gem install), the validator id docs_capability, the finding term id unattributable_failure, spec 2 §3/§7 citations, the defect-lineage tickets (#1745, #1774, #1716) with their rule/check names, and the companion rule slugs .render-builds and .internal-refs-resolve (generalized in doesNotFire to descriptive references, since sibling rule ids belong to this rule family's realization).
